reasons.claim: The two shaykhs of Sa'd are co-transmitters joined by «جميعا» before Ibn Abi Umayr, as both readers put them in one level.
reasons.quote: جَمِيعاً عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ

reasons.claim: The two Imams are joint last links who speak together, so they are alternatives in the last level.
reasons.quote: عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ الْبَاقِرِ وَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الصَّادِقِ ع قَالا

reasons.claim: Abd al-Azim asks the Imam, who answers, so the Imam named in the words after the chain is the last link (rulings 2 and 3).
reasons.quote: قُلْتُ لِمُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُوسَى ع

reasons.claim: Mu'awiya and an unnamed «غيره» transmit side by side from the Imam, giving one narrator and one unnamed alternative in one level.
reasons.quote: عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ وَهْبٍ وَ غَيْرِهِ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا

reasons.claim: The chain runs to the Imam after «عن» and the asker of «سألته» is the preceding link Zurara, so no link is missing after the Imam.
reasons.quote: عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ

reasons.claim: The first-person question is the narrator's own question to the Imam, a normal asker-answer form, not an open question.
Two co-transmitters joined by «و» narrate from the Imam, giving two routes.
reasons.quote: أَبُو اَلْعَبَّاسِ وَ عُبَيْدٌ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ

reviews.question: An Imam's saying stated by the compiler with no transmitter (close to the unruled «قضى أمير المؤمنين … في» with no transmitter).

reasons.claim: No transmitter stands before the scene; Ali is the one who speaks, so if such reports keep the speaker as the sole link the reading is right, and if the owner rules them chainless it would become no_chain.
reasons.quote: وَ رَأَى عَلِيٌّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مَسْجِداً

reviews.uncertainty_note: Whether a transmitter-less Imam's saying is stored as a one-link chain or as no_chain is unruled.

reasons.claim: Ali is asked and answers in the words after the chain, so he is the last link after the relation «أبيه».
reasons.quote: أَنَّ عَلِيَّ بْنَ أَبِي طَالِبٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ سُئِلَ

reasons.claim: The chain opens with the bare relation «أبي» as the compiler's shaykh.
Isa addresses the Imam, who answers, so the Imam is the last link; the stored chain wrongly drops Abd al-Azim and the Imam.
Isma'il narrates from a bare «أبيه», who then narrates from al-Rida, so the relation is its own link.
The chain ends at Abu Talib, who relays what the Prophet did and said; the Prophet is not a link.

reviews.uncertainty_note: Reader B's expanded surface for the Ali link reads «عَلَيْ», a matching glitch; the structure is the same as reader A's.

reasons.claim: One transmitter narrates from the Imam, who answers; the stored chain's Quranic word is not a link.
reasons.quote: وَ رَوَى أَبَانُ بْنُ تَغْلِبَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ
